wording: - **Employers in Germany.** Wage tax is collected by deduction from pay where the employer is a "domestic employer": it has a residence, seat, management, permanent establishment or permanent representative in Germany, or it is a foreign agency hiring out workers to work in Germany ([§ 38(1) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__38.html)). wording: **Minijob rules.** The limit is on regular monthly pay; an unforeseeable overrun in not more than two calendar months within the twelve months ending with the pay period, each by up to the limit itself, does not end the Minijob ([§ 8(1b) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__8.html)). A Minijobber is in pension insurance unless they apply in writing or electronically to be released ([§ 6(1b) SGB VI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_6/__6.html)); the employer's 15% stays. The flat tax is an option: the employer may tax by the ELStAM instead. The 2% flat tax is collected by the Minijob-Zentrale (Deutsche Rentenversicherung Knappschaft-Bahn-See, [§ 40a(6) EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__40a.html)); 20% and 25% go on the wage tax return. Exactly EUR 603 is a Minijob ("nicht übersteigt"); EUR 603.01 is in the transition band. If aggregation shows that the minor-employment conditions fail, insurance begins on the day the competent insurance decision is notified under § 8(2) SGB IV, unless the employer intentionally or grossly negligently failed to investigate the facts needed to assess insurance status. This is the specific aggregation rule, not a universal bar on retroactive insurance.

Contributions are worked out on reduced bases by two formulas in [§ 20(2a) SGB IV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_4/__20.html), with AE the monthly pay, G = EUR 603 and F = 0.6619. For the ordinarily shared branches outside Saxony, compute the total contribution by applying half the contribution rate to the first base, rounding to cents and doubling; compute the employee's ordinary half-rate contribution on the second base, rounding to cents. The employer bears the difference. Calculate the employee-only childless care surcharge on the first base; calculate care reductions on the second base, each rounded separately ([§ 1(2) and § 2(2) BVV](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/beitrvv/__2.html)). Saxony has a separate allocation under § 58(5) SGB XI; this ordinary half-rate worksheet does not supply that Saxony allocation. At AE EUR 1,000 the bases are EUR 854.06 and EUR 568.36. Not for apprentices. Exactly EUR 2,000 is still in the band ("nicht übersteigen").

wording: **Sick pay and the maternity top-up.** Continued pay for up to six weeks per incapacity due to sickness without employee fault, once the job has lasted four weeks without a break; the same illness again gives a new six weeks only after six months free of it, or twelve months after the first incapacity from it began ([§ 3 EntgFG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__3.html)), at the pay for regular working time ([§ 4 EntgFG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__4.html)). During the protection periods and the day of birth the employer pays the difference between EUR 13 and the average net pay per calendar day from the last three settled calendar months before the protection period ([§ 20(1) MuSchG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/muschg_2018/__20.html)); U2 refunds it ([§ 1(2) AAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/aufag/__1.html)). Under § 4(1a) EntgFG, additional overtime pay is excluded, as are expense reimbursements contingent on actual expenses that do not arise during incapacity. For performance-related remuneration, use the average earnings achievable during the employee's applicable regular working time. For the ordinary multiple-employer case, add the relevant employers' average daily net wages, subtract EUR 13 once, then allocate that top-up in proportion to each employer's average daily net wage. At independently established daily net EUR 60 and EUR 40, combined EUR 100 less EUR 13 gives EUR 87; employer shares are EUR 52.20 and EUR 34.80, not two separate EUR 13 deductions. The ordinary worksheet assumes ongoing employment and established § 20 net inputs. New employment begun during protection is covered from its start under § 20(1); the specific authorised-dismissal/insolvency cases shift payment to the statutory paying agency under § 20(3). For treaty non-residents whose residence state has the taxing right, § 20(4) uses only social-insurance deductions unless that state does not tax the top-up, in which case all statutory deductions count. This is not a full § 21 proof of each real net-pay input.

### Example 1: class I, EUR 5,000 a month, childless, outside Saxony

An employee aged 30, no church, no children, place of employment in Hesse, statutory health fund with a 2.9% additional rate, EUR 5,000 a month, no one-time payments. Annual pay is EUR 60,000. The Vorsorgepauschale is pension EUR 5,580 (60,000 x 9.3%) plus health and care EUR 6,510 (60,000 x (1.45% + 7.0% + 2.4%)). Health and care alone pass EUR 1,900, so unemployment adds nothing: EUR 12,090. The taxable amount is 60,000 less 1,230 less 36 less 12,090 = EUR 46,644, in the second progressive zone. The tariff gives EUR 9,389 a year, the ministry's test-table figure, so EUR 782.41 a month. No surcharge: EUR 9,389 is under EUR 20,350. Employee contributions are pension EUR 465.00, unemployment EUR 65.00, health EUR 437.50 (half of 17.5%) and care EUR 120.00 (2.4%). Net pay is EUR 3,130.09. The employer adds its own EUR 465.00, 65.00, 437.50 and EUR 90.00 care, plus the 0.15% insolvency levy and U1 and U2.
